# Künneth formula for group cohomology with U(1) coefficients# For a direct product G = H x K, with K = Z_13 of prime order 13:# Notice that |H| = 48 = 2^4 * 3.# The orders of H and K are COPRIME:# gcd(|H|, |K|) = gcd(48, 13) = 1!# A fundamental theorem of group cohomology for finite groups of coprime orders:# For any two finite groups H and K with gcd(|H|, |K|) = 1:# H^n(H x K, M) \cong H^n(H, M) \oplus H^n(K, M) for any trivial module M where |M| is not divisible by orders, or for U(1)!# Let's verify this theorem!# For any finite group G, H^n(G, U(1)) is an abelian group annihilated by |G|:# |G| * H^n(G, U(1)) = 0.# Thus, for any prime p, the p-primary component of H^n(G, U(1)) is isomorphic to the p-primary component of H^n(G_p, U(1)) (where G_p is Sylow p-subgroup), etc.# In particular, for G = H x K with gcd(|H|, |K|) = 1:# The Sylow p-subgroups of G are:# - for p | |H| (p = 2, 3): Sylow subgroups of H.# - for p = 13: Sylow 13-subgroup of K (which is Z_13).# Since Sylow subgroups for different primes are completely decoupled:# The p-primary part of H^n(H x K, U(1)) comes ENTIRELY from H for p in {2, 3},# and ENTIRELY from K for p = 13!# That means:# H^n(H x K, U(1)) \cong H^n(H, U(1)) \oplus H^n(K, U(1)) !# FOR ALL n >= 1 !# That is an exact theorem!print("Coprime group cohomology splitting holds identically!")
